key_insight: A single intravenous AAV9-GLB1 gene transfer was associated with sustained clinical, biochemical, and neuroimaging improvement in a juvenile GM1 gangliosidosis participant over multi-year follow-up.
clinical_relevance: This expanded-access case suggests that gene therapy may provide meaningful benefit even in advanced neurodegenerative lysosomal disease, though broader confirmation is needed.
method: Longitudinal follow-up for 5 years of safety and 3 years of efficacy
Clinical, biochemical, and neuroimaging assessments tracked over time
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a single-participant longitudinal evaluation with seizure, adaptive-function, CSF biomarker, enzyme activity, and MRI/tractography outcomes improving after treatment.
watch_item: Because this is a single-patient expanded-access report, the apparent benefits may not generalize and causality cannot be firmly established.
paper_title: Expanded Access use of Intravenous Gene Transfer with AAV9-GLB1 in a Juvenile GM1 Gangliosidosis Participant
